real: Hundreds of people in a French city start dancing uncontrollably for a month
source: 1518 — the Dancing Plague of Strasbourg: reports describe a woman stepping into a street to dance, followed within a day by dozens, then hundreds, who danced for weeks into exhaustion and, in some accounts, death — with no clear cause ever established.
fakes: A mysterious illness makes an entire city dance for weeks

real: The U.S. and Britain nearly go to war over a single shot pig
source: 1859 — the Pig War: a U.S. settler shot a British-owned pig on disputed territory between the U.S. and Britain, and both nations mobilized troops, bringing the two countries to the brink of war over a pot of pork.
fakes: A border dispute between two nations is triggered by a farm animal

real: Two Italian cities go to war over a stolen wooden bucket
source: The War of the Bucket (1325) — the cities of Bologna and Modena fought a bitter war whose trigger, according to tradition, was a stolen ceremonial wooden bucket, which Bologna still keeps on display as a trophy.
fakes: A centuries-old feud between two cities began over a single object

real: In the final days of WWII, German and American soldiers fight together against the Nazis
source: 1945 — the Battle of Castle Itter: in a bizarre last week of the war, Wehrmacht and Waffen-SS soldiers joined forces with U.S. troops to defend a castle holding rescued French war ministers, defeating the Waffen-SS in what is one of the few times the two sides fought as allies.
fakes: Allied and German soldiers briefly become allies in the war's final days

real: The smell of London's river is so bad that MPs refuse to go to work
source: 1858 — the Great Stink: the River Thames smelled so foul from untreated sewage in a hot summer that members of Parliament sealed the windows with lime and the government, for once, acted fast, commissioning a modern sewer system for the city.
fakes: A city's river becomes so polluted it shuts down the seat of government

real: A volcano's ash causes a year with no summer — and changes world history
source: 1816 — the 'Year Without a Summer': the 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora cooled the planet so much that New England saw frost in June, harvests failed worldwide, and the misery is often cited as a factor behind Mary Shelley writing Frankenstein.
fakes: A volcanic eruption turns a summer into a winter across a continent

real: Thousands of strange tiles with a riddle are embedded in city streets
source: The Toynbee Tiles — hundreds of concrete tiles bearing the riddle 'TOYNBEE — TO BUILD A WORLD RELIGION — CONTACT' have been embedded into street corners across dozens of cities, apparently by a single anonymous person, with no one ever confirming the story behind them.
fakes: A mysterious message appears carved into streets across many cities

real: Nine hikers die in the Ural Mountains under conditions that remain a mystery
source: 1959 — the Dyatlov Pass incident: nine experienced hikers were found dead in the Urals, their tent cut from inside, some without shoes or clothes in sub-zero temperatures, and the official file was classified for years — one of the most enduring unsolved mysteries in history.
fakes: A group of hikers perishes in the mountains in circumstances no one can explain

real: A 46-foot stone giant is discovered under a hill in Wales — until it's not
source: The Cardiff Giant — a 46-foot (14 m) stone 'giant' was unveiled as a 'recent discovery' under a hill in Cardiff in 1869 and drew thousands of curious visitors, until the sculptor admitted he'd carved and buried it himself as a publicity stunt.

real: Two girls 'photograph' fairies, and the famous author believes them
source: The Cottingley Fairies — in 1917, two young girls in England photographed themselves with paper 'fairies,' and the images convinced Sir Arthur Conan Doyle and others for decades that real fairies existed, before the girls confessed the trick in 1983.

real: A French soldier eats so much, constantly, that doctors study him
source: Tarrare — an 18th-century French soldier reportedly ate 12 pounds (5 kg) of food a day, along with stones, insects, and live animals, and was eventually 'used' by the military as a living courier who could hide messages in his stomach, becoming a subject of medical fascination.

real: A knot of dead rats found in a sewer turns out to be a real biological thing
source: The 'rat king' — a phenomenon in which several dead rats become tangled together by their fur into a single knot, found in sewers and attics, is a real (if gruesome) occurrence documented since the 1890s, with specimens in museums and an annual 'rat king of the year' contest in some quarters.
